transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess the main thing is I just can’t seem to sit still when I’m supposed to. It feels like there’s a motor running under my skin, especially in staff meetings or at church briefings. I end up shifting around, standing up, or finding some reason to go move.
Can you describe how often this restlessness or urge to move happens? Is it something you feel most days, or does it come and go?

It’s pretty frequent. I’d say most days, especially any time I’m expected to sit still for a while. In staff meetings or church briefings, I feel that humming, like I’ve got to move, and I start shifting around or standing up, or I’ll look for some reason to step away.
Do you also feel this restlessness or need to move when you're not in meetings or church briefings, like when you're at home relaxing or trying to focus on a task by yourself?

Yeah, it’s not just meetings. On my shifts I’m always bouncing from one thing to the next—mopping, then checking trash, then straightening chairs—without really stopping. And when I get home, instead of sitting down after work, I’ll start puttering around in the garage or re-sorting tools. It’s like I have a hard time just being still.
Do you also find it hard to focus or concentrate on tasks, like following through on something you start or staying attentive when someone’s talking to you?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I can listen when someone’s talking to me, and I usually get my work done. I haven’t noticed that being the main problem so much as just feeling like I need to be moving.
Do you ever feel anxious, worried, or on edge, especially in situations where you're expected to sit still or stay focused?

I don’t know if I’d call it anxious, really. I’m not sitting there worrying about something bad happening. It’s more like I get uncomfortable or keyed up when I have to stay still. Like my body wants to get up and move, but I wouldn’t say it feels like worry exactly.
Do you also feel this restlessness or need to move in other situations, like when you’re out with friends or family, or during downtime when you’re not working or at church?

Yeah, it happens there too. Like if I’m fishing with my wife, I’m supposed to be relaxing, but I’ll be tapping my foot or messing with my tackle box over and over. Or at bingo, I’ll catch myself fidgeting with the pencil, talking too loud, that kind of thing. It’s hard for me to just sit quiet and enjoy it sometimes.
When did you first notice these feelings of restlessness and the need to keep moving? Were you like this even as a child, or did it start more recently?

It goes back pretty far, honestly. I remember in grade school getting in trouble for jumping up out of my seat, talking over the teacher, or starting on things before she even finished giving directions. My mother used to say I was wound too tight even back then.
Can you recall times when you had trouble staying focused or had to put in extra effort to keep your attention on something, even if it wasn’t because you were anxious or worried?

I’m not sure. I mean, I know I get restless, but as far as focus goes… I’d have to think about that. I don’t want to say something just to say it. Nothing specific is coming to mind right now where it felt separate from just needing to move around.

Have you ever had times when it was hard for you to stay focused on what someone was saying, or when you found yourself missing details or making careless mistakes, even if it wasn’t because you were restless or anxious?

I don’t really know. I can’t think of a clear example like that. I mean, if I miss something someone says, it’s usually because I’m getting antsy or wanting to move around, not just because my mind drifts off. So… nothing specific comes to mind with careless mistakes or missing details on its own.
Have you ever found yourself acting without thinking, blurting things out, or interrupting others, especially in situations where you’re expected to wait your turn or listen?

Yes, that does happen. Like when my supervisor at work, or sometimes someone at church, starts giving me instructions, I’ll jump in before they’re done because I think I know what they’re about to say. Then sometimes I’m wrong, and they have to stop me and correct me. It’s not like I mean to be rude, I just answer too fast.
